From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Brightleaf - post-demo security recap & SIG prefill

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the pilot and procurement timeline.

Call highlights (from our side):
- Brightleaf interested in hosted API with VPC egress and SOC 2 + HIPAA controls; pilot scope = de-identified analytics (no PHI expected, but you said some workflows may touch limited PHI).
- Primary concerns: SOC 2 status, data residency for PHI, BAA requirement, audit/log access for the pilot, and subprocessor list.

Action items / asks:
1) We attached a short SIG prefill worksheet (Brightleaf_SIG_prefill_v1.xlsx) — can you complete the marked tabs with any existing answers you can share (SOC 2 report date, required evidence contact, preferred SIG format: SIG Lite / Full SIG / CAIQ)?
2) Clarify whether Brightleaf will require a BAA for the pilot. If yes, please indicate procurement contact for legal redlines.
3) Confirm desired data residency (US-east, US-west, or EU) and whether you need dedicated VPC/private deployment for the pilot.
4) Please share the security contact (if different from this thread) who can own evidence exchange and technical calls.

Ben and Rishi are looped in — Ben will be the technical security SME and Rishi will coordinate any SOC 2 / compliance evidence.

Next steps I propose:
- If you can return the prefill by end of week, Ben and I will schedule a 30-min security intake to walk gaps and timeline.
- We will attach a Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Brightleaf_RWD-3421.pdf) to keep dates aligned with procurement.

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,

Hi Sarah — Ben from Redwood Security here. Thanks for the demo today, good overview. A couple of technical clarifying questions so we can complete our side of the SIG and map evidence options:

1) Encryption/key management: will Brightleaf require customer-managed keys (BYOK/KMS) for the pilot or is provider-managed encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+/in transit) acceptable?
2) Audit logs / access: do you need real-time access to request/response logs, or is periodic export (daily/weekly) sufficient for your audit needs? If real-time, can you confirm the retention window required (days/months)?
3) Data classification / PHI: you mentioned some ingestion pipelines may contain limited PHI. Can you confirm if PHI fields will be stripped before calling the API, or if they will be sent encrypted to an isolated Redwood tenant?
4) Subprocessors: do you have any blockers for us sharing our subprocessor list; if so, please flag that now so we can arrange an NDA or controlled disclosure.

If you prefer, we can review these items during a technical intake call — I expect ~30 minutes. Tentative availability Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Brightleaf - post-demo security recap & SIG prefill

Marissa / Ben — thank you, appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline:

- SIG prefill: attaching an initial set (Brightleaf_SIG_prefill_v1.xlsx). We've filled the SOC 2 status (Type II, last audit 2025-11) and indicated preferred SIG format as SIG Lite to start. The full evidence package will require a controlled exchange.
- BAA: Brightleaf's legal team typically requires a BAA for any vendor that may process PHI. For the pilot, we can scope to de-identified analytics but procurement wants the BAA option to be available. Procurement contact: Liam O'Neill (liam.oneill@brightleaf.com).
- Data residency: US-east preferred. For the pilot we do not require dedicated on-prem; a dedicated VPC in US-east would be ideal.
- Logs: We need request-level logs available on a 7-day retention window initially and daily exports to our S3 for audits. Real-time push is not required for phase 1.
- Encryption: Provider-managed keys are OK for pilot; if we move to production we will evaluate BYOK.
- Subprocessors: we can accept a redacted subprocessors list initially; full details require an NDA.

We'll schedule a technical intake — Liam and our security mailbox (it-security@brightleaf.com) will coordinate availability.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of Security Programs, Brightleaf Health
